request: How large is the immigration court backlog, and how has it changed?

reply.reply:
At the end of FY2024, the immigration-court backlog stood at **3,558,995 pending cases**. It had already exceeded **1.5 million** in the first quarter of FY2022, showing a steep increase over that period (CRS R47077, PDF p. 21; CRS IN12492, PDF p. 4).

The flow of cases helps explain the growth: in FY2024, EOIR received an average of 148,663 new cases per month, while judges completed an average of 58,479 per month (CRS IN12492, PDF p. 4).

See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-180811-76cb.html) for details and citations.
reply.reasoning: The latest verified backlog figure is the FY2024-end total. The comparable historical evidence shows more than 1.5 million cases in FY2022 Q1, while current receipts substantially outpaced completions.
